schema: CREATE TABLE doctors (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT); CREATE TABLE appointments (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, doctor_id INTEGER, patient_id INTEGER, FOREIGN KEY (patient_id) REFERENCES patients(id), FOREIGN KEY (doctor_id) REFERENCES doctors(id)); CREATE TABLE patients (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT);
correct_query: SELECT d.name, p.name FROM doctors d LEFT JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id LEFT JOIN patients p ON a.patient_id = p.id;

expected_semantic_errors_to_be_caught.description: Model utilizes an INNER JOIN across all tables, incorrectly excluding doctors that currently have no scheduled appointments.
expected_semantic_errors_to_be_caught.query: SELECT d.name, p.name FROM doctors d INNER JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id INNER JOIN patients p ON a.patient_id = p.id;

expected_semantic_errors_to_be_caught.description: Model correctly LEFT JOINs appointments but follows it with an INNER JOIN on patients, which structurally negates the preceding LEFT JOIN's inclusivity.
expected_semantic_errors_to_be_caught.query: SELECT d.name, p.name FROM doctors d LEFT JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id INNER JOIN patients p ON a.patient_id = p.id;
SELECT d.name, p.name FROM doctors d JOIN appointments a ON d.id = a.doctor_id JOIN patients p ON a.patient_id = p.id;
